messages.subject: stochastic map output /simmap question
messages.body_plain:
Howdy all,

I'm writing to find out if anyone knows of any scripts that can convert the ana.events and clado.events tables from a BGB stochastic mapping output into the ‘simmap’ format of phytools (i.e., a phylo object with additional entries ‘$maps’ and ‘$mapped.edge’ describing the state of each branch)? I’m hoping to use some model-fitting tools that were designed for simmap objects, but before diving in to script writing, I thought I’d check to see whether there are any existing tools that could help.

Thanks in advance!

Jonathan Drury

messages.subject: time stratified analysis - time slices in wrong place
messages.subject_clean: time stratified analysis - time slices in wrong place
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick,
using your example script as a template, I have attempted to run a time stratified analysis. All input file formats are corresponding with your templates. However, in the PDF output, the time slices as indicated by dashed lines are not in the place where they should be according to the definitions of the input file timeperiods.txt (0.1 - 0.24 - 0.47 - 0.66 - 0.83 - 1.1). Instead, they all sit much deeper in time. My question: Is this a problem relating to the drawing of the PDF graphic or does this indicate that the time slices are somehow incorrectly applied in the analyses. And how can I fix this? Thanks, Frank (Attachments: Biogeobears skript, timeperiods.txt, PDF output example)

Hi Nick, Torsten and all,

I wish to use an areas allowed matrix and I found this topic which helped me a lot.

However, I could not successfully run the analyse : I still get estimations for the ranges I disallowed.

Using your function on my dataset, Torsten, I get the following error :
Error in calc_loglike_sp(tip_condlikes_of_data_on_each_state = subtree_tip_relative_probs_of_each_state,  :
  object 'printlevel' not found

Did you get this kind of errors ?

@Nick, do you have implemented the code to your package or should I try to understand what is wrong with my data ?

All the best,

Pierre

messages.body_plain:
Hi Frank -- thanks for sending the files.

The issue is just this: your input tree had a root.edge, you can see it if you do:

trfn = ("mcmc_tree.tre")
tr = read.tree(trfn)
names(tr)

You can remove it if you do:
tr$root.edge = NULL
write.tree(tr, file="mcmc_tree2.tre")

...and use that as the new input tree.

It looks like the plotting function (which has to convert ages-before-present into ages-from-the-bottom-of-the-tree) mistakenly assumes that the bottom of the tree will always be the root node, rather than the bottom of the root edge.

I can fix this at some point, but for now it is easier to fix your tree.  This error is just about plotting, so the base analysis should not be effected.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hey Nick,

I have a tree that is massive (>9000 tips, with 11 ranges) that will predictably not fit in BioGeoBEARS. However, I think it will run in the C++ version of LaGrange.

My hope is that I could use the maximum likelihood parameter estimates for the DEC model from LaGrange and then pass those to BioGeoBEARS to build stochastic maps from this model fit.

I think it would be straightforward to edit the res$outputs to incorporate the estimates from LaGrange, but studying the stochastic mapping scripts for a stratified analysis, it looks like stochastic mapping also requires the res$condlikes_table, res$relative_probs_of_each_state_at_branch_[...]_DOWNPASS_TABLE, res$ML_marginal_prob[...]_bottom_below_node, and res$ML_marginal_prob[...]_top_AT_node.

My question then, is whether it would be theoretically possible to get these tables somehow if I know the maximum likelihood parameter estimates from the DEC model already.

Thanks again for your help,

Jonathan

Hi- on my phone at the moment, but briefly, in general it would be easy, but if you are having a memory error or whatever, then that would occur just the same for calculating the likelihood and ancestral state probabilities once for one set of user -specified parameters, as for doing a full ML analysis.

Basically, imagine storing in memory a table that has 2*ntips-1 rows and numstates colums , that might be 18,000*2000 for your case. Or the issue could be with parallelization, where it stores P matrices for all 18000 branches. Turning off parallelization would be the solution in thats case. There might be a way to up the memory alotment for R, if you know the error message we could explore more.

The easiest solution would likely be do compromise a little on the max number of areas and reduce the state space.
Cheers, nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Some things to try:

1. Make sure library(snow) and/or library(parallel) work in your R terminal.

2. Make sure you're using this script, not another one:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

3. ...in that script, run the lines in small chunks at first espeically make sure all the source() commands run

...cheers!
Ncik
